claim.pdf_says: DISPLAY Format 2 prints the AT phrase with choice-indicator bars inside its brace and the exception phrase with choice-indicator bars inside its bracket (both verified on the enlarged crop).
claim.markdown_says: > **Figure notes -- choice indicators (ISO 5.2.6.4).** Two groups in this format carry choice-indicator bars, both lost in transcription.  -- while the code block directly above it DOES render them: '⎧|                ⎧ identifier-2 ⎫             |⎫' and '⎡|  ON EXCEPTION imperative-statement-1      |⎤'
claim.why_it_matters: The figure note contradicts the diagram it annotates: it declares the bars 'lost in transcription' when the accompanying ASCII diagram correctly preserves them. A later reader or repair pass may believe this figure is still defective and 'fix' an already-correct diagram, or conversely conclude the bars in the diagram are spurious. This is the only note in the batch that describes the transcription's own history rather than the printed standard.

verdict.reasoning:
Independently verified against both sources; the claim survives every refutation test I applied.

(1) PDF, page 640 (printed folio 610), section 14.9.11.2 Format 2 (screen). I rendered at 300 dpi and cropped/upscaled both groups. AT phrase: reading left to right the printed glyph stack is an outer square bracket '[', then a brace '{', then a full-height straight vertical rule; on the right side a matching full-height vertical rule, then '}', then ']'. Exception phrase: '[' then a vertical rule, the two stacked ON EXCEPTION / NOT ON EXCEPTION lines, then a vertical rule, then ']'. Those inner straight rules are unmistakably distinct from the curly brace/square bracket strokes that flank them -- they are the ISO 5.2.6.4 choice indicators. So the PDF half of the claim is exactly as stated.

(2) Markdown. The extracted page-640.md and the canonical specs/ISO_COBOL.md (lines 26499-26514) agree byte for byte. The code block DOES carry both bar groups: line '⎡    ⎧|                ⎧ identifier-2 ⎫             |⎫ ⎤' and the four AT continuation lines each place '|' immediately inside the brace column and again immediately inside the closing brace column; the exception group is '⎡|  ON EXCEPTION imperative-statement-1      |⎤' / '⎣|  NOT ON EXCEPTION imperative-statement-2  |⎦'. So the transcription is FAITHFUL -- nothing from the printed figure was lost.

(3) The prose note immediately below nonetheless asserts 'Two groups in this format carry choice-indicator bars, both lost in transcription.' That sentence is false about the document that contains it. The claim quotes it accurately (the only deviation is rendering the em dash as '--'), and quotes the two code lines accurately as substrings.

Refutation tests, all failed to refute: the text is not merely reflowed or on an adjacent line (there is nothing to find -- the note asserts an absence that does not exist); it is not page-break furniture, wrapping, hyphenation, or formatting; neither source is misquoted.

On 'does it change meaning': it does not corrupt any COBOL semantics -- items (1) and (2) of the note correctly describe one-or-more-in-any-order for the braced AT group and zero-or-more-in-any-order for the bracketed exception group, matching what the diagram already encodes, and the 'Underlined required words' list (DISPLAY, LINE, COLUMN, COL, EXCEPTION, NOT, END-DISPLAY) checks out against the PDF, with the optional word NUMBER correctly omitted. But the sentence still states a falsehood about the transcription's own state, and it is stale in a directional way: it invites a future repair pass to 'restore' bars that are already there, or to delete the existing '|' glyphs as noise.

Corroborating evidence that this is an outlier rather than a house convention: 'lost in transcription' occurs exactly ONCE in the whole of specs/ISO_COBOL.md (line 26511). Every sibling choice-indicator note describes the PRINTED standard and reports a verification, e.g. line 16242 'The bracket is plain -- re-rendered at 600 dpi and confirmed to carry **no** choice-indicator bars', line 19860 'no choice indicators -- verified at 600 dpi', line 26850 'Verified at 900 dpi: NO choice-indicator bars are present.' This note alone reports on the transcription's own history, and reports it wrongly.
verdict.corrected_description: Real, but narrower than 'a PDF-vs-markdown fidelity defect'. The transcription of the standard is CORRECT and COMPLETE: page 640 / section 14.9.11.2 Format 2 prints choice-indicator bars inside the AT brace and inside the exception bracket, and the markdown code block reproduces both groups as '|'. The defect is confined to one clause of the transcriber's annotation directly beneath the diagram, which says the bars were 'both lost in transcription' -- a stale, self-contradictory statement about the markdown itself, not a misstatement of ISO. Fix is a single clause: replace 'both lost in transcription' with a statement of what was verified and preserved (e.g. 'both verified on the rendered page and preserved above as "|"'), matching the house style used at ISO_COBOL.md lines 16242, 19860 and 26850. The remainder of the note -- the (1) braces = one-or-more-any-order and (2) brackets = zero-or-more-any-order readings, and the underlined-required-words list -- is accurate against the PDF and must be left intact. No change to the ASCII diagram is warranted; the risk this finding guards against is precisely that someone edits the already-correct diagram.
